finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return, so the OWNER check never runs and any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe; the User argument and tenant path parameter are caller-controlled (src/Admin.java:24-25)

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called with return value discarded
requireRole returns a boolean and never throws, so the call is a no-op

finding.guards_checked: Only control on path is requireRole at line 26; its result is unused, so it is not enforced. No tenant-ownership check exists. Sibling export() uses checkRole (throws) at line 32, which shows the intended pattern.

verdict.guard_found: Only candidate control is requireRole at src/Admin.java:26, which returns a boolean (src/Admin.java:14-16, "Does not throw") and is called as a bare statement, so its result is discarded and nothing is enforced. No tenant-ownership check exists anywhere in the repo. The sibling export() at src/Admin.java:32 uses checkRole (throws, src/Admin.java:18-22), which is the enforcing pattern and is not used here.
verdict.reason: At src/Admin.java:26 the boolean from requireRole is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any User that reaches wipe(), including one without the OWNER role. Caveat: the repo contains no router or auth layer, so how the User argument is built from the HTTP request is unverified; the finding holds for any caller that reaches wipe() with a non-OWNER user.

finding.claim: UNCERTAIN: export() checks a global OWNER role but never ties it to the requested tenant, because User has no tenant field; a user with OWNER on tenant A may export tenant B if roles are global.
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/export; tenant path parameter is caller-controlled (src/Admin.java:30-31)

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) entry point

User record has no tenant field, so role scope cannot be verified here

finding.guards_checked: checkRole at line 32 throws correctly for missing role. No tenant-to-user binding exists in this repo. Repo implementation and User construction are not present, so this cannot be confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:32 is a real guard: it throws SecurityException when the user lacks "OWNER". It is not tenant-aware, and no tenant-to-user binding exists in src/Admin.java (User at line 4 is a record of name and roles only). The repo implementation of export and any upstream scoping of User are not in the directory.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches (src/Admin.java:30-33), and checkRole at line 32 is effective but has no tenant check, so an OWNER on one tenant could reach repo.export on another. Whether that is exploitable depends on whether role sets are tenant-scoped before reaching this method, and the caller and repo code that would show this are absent, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from this directory.
